glosses: oh! (expresses surprise or realization)

Expression of surprise.

examples.text: Oh! I didn't see you there.

glosses: Expression of wonder, amazement, or awe.

examples.text: Oh, wow! That's amazing.

glosses: Expression of understanding, affirmation, recognition, or realization.

examples.text: Oh, so that's how it works.

glosses: A word to precede an offhand or annoyed remark.

examples.text: Oh, leave me alone.

glosses: A word to precede an added comment or afterthought.

examples.text: Oh, and don't forget your coat.

glosses: An invocation or address (similar to the vocative in languages with noun declension), often with a term of endearment.

examples.text: Oh, gosh
Oh baby, baby, how was I supposed to know / That something wasn't right here?

glosses: Exclamation for drama or emphasis (often poetic).

examples.text: Oh, when will it end?

And oh how stingingly acute, and pungently grievous and tormentive, are the remembrancing Reflections of a separate uncloathed Soul in the other World, upon a review of its mad Choice, foolish Hopes, fruitless Desires […]

Oh, by what plots, by what forswearings, betrayings, oppressions, imprisonments, tortures, poisonings, and under what reasons of state and politic subtilty, have these forenamed kings […] pulled the vengeance of God upon themselves […]

glosses: Expression of pain. See ouch.

examples.text: Oh! That hurt.
"Oh! . . . oh! . . . I can't bear it . . . It is too much . . . I die . . . I am going . . ." were Polly's expressions of extasy

glosses: Space filler or extra syllable, especially in (popular) music.

examples.text: I'm off with the raggle-taggle gypsy-oh.

glosses: Expression of mild scepticism.

examples.text: "You should watch where you're going!" "Oh?"

glosses: A word to mark a spoken phrase as imaginary.

examples.text: What if he says "Oh, I need to see your ID"?

glosses: An utterance of oh; a spoken expression of surprise, acknowledgement, etc.

examples.text: There were ohs and ahs, and the people twisted about as they looked for her. Then they began to applaud.

glosses: To utter the interjection oh; to express surprise, etc.

examples.text: A quarter of an hour elapsed, and then, after several rings at the door-bell, a smothered laugh, and a good deal of ohing and ahing, the door was thrown open, and one by one, as they were announced, in came the expected characters.

glosses: The name of the Latin-script letter O/o.

glosses: To give a cry of \"ah\".

examples.text: Mother and dad oohed and ahed over Cindy. She was only two months old but already was developing her personality.

glosses: Pronunciation spelling of I, most often indicating that the speaker is using a Scottish or American (particularly Southern) accent or African-American Vernacular English.

examples.text: Did ah ever say anything derogatory against ma man Franco? Well, likesay. . . he's no a bad punter.

glosses: Marks a yes–no tag question prompting the listener to clarify or confirm something.

examples.text: Pitch contour: low-mid /ɑ(ː)˨/, [ä˨]
You’re dyslexic ah?
So how are you Jackson? Very busy, ah? Never come around to see me these days.
Cannot talk-ah? God give you mouth for what? No courtesy-ah? Kanneena!

examples.text: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/
How do you delete this row ah?
See how lor. Who’s going ar?

glosses: Emphasizes the need for absolute confirmation, permission or acknowledgment.

examples.text: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/

glosses: A particle indicating the topic of a sentence from its comment.

examples.text: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/

These fish, ah, anything also eat one.

glosses: A confirmative final particle used in the middle of a sentence to ascertain the continued attention of the listener.

examples.text: Pitch contour: rising /ɑ(ː)˨˦/
Near-synonym: right
You know, arh, Isaac—I’ve liked you from the very start, he said. I consider myself very lucky to be your manager.

glosses: Tagged at the end of non-interrogative sentence to convey a sense of informality or resignation.

examples.text: Pitch contour: mid-falling /ɑ(ː)˧˨/
I got tell them ah, guys.

glosses: Reinforces a short, sarcastic suggestion.

glosses: A vocative particle, now mostly used by Chinese elders for direct address (over telephone calls, or if the addressee is far away).

examples.text: Pitch contour: low-mid /ɑ(ː)˨/
